newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada committee urges phasing in tobacco rules.
newsitem.headline: Canada committee urges phasing in tobacco rules.

text.p: The Canadian House of Commons Health Committee recommended on Thursday phasing in planned restrictions on tobacco sponsorship of sporting and other events rather than introducing them immediately.

The restrictions are part of an anti-tobacco bill which the government hopes to push through the House, Parliament's elected chamber, early next year. The sponsorship restrictions have prompted warnings that sports events or festivals could collapse.

Committee Chairman Roger Simmons said "a phased-in period would help minimize any adverse impact the bill might otherwise have on sponsored events, while at the same time facilitating the health objectives of the legislation."
A statement from the committee said it recommended that Health Minister David Dingwall consider amendments which "would provide transitional provisions relating to sponsorship."
Dingwall has said he was willing to listen to such a request.
Canada's tobacco industry is about 65 percent-controlled by Imperial Tobacco Ltd, a unit of Imasco Ltd. Imasco is 40 percent-owned by Britain's B.A.T. Industries Plc.

Another big Canadian cigarette company is Rothmans, Benson and Hedges Inc, 60 percent-owned by Rothmans Inc -- a unit of Rothmans International Plc -- and 40 percent by Philip Morris Cos Inc. A third major player is RJR MacDonald, wholly owned by RJR Nabisco Holdings Corp unit R.J. Reynolds Tobacco International.
